title: Connection quarantine and transparent replay safeguard for hosted API escalations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a recent customer escalation we observed correlated 5xx spikes and long-tail timeouts from hosted API frontends. Investigation shows a composite failure mode: transient kernel-scheduling stalls on GPU workers combined with aggressive client retries caused KV cache churn and connection thrash. This ticket implements a connection-level tenant quarantine and a transparent-replay safeguard so we can (a) stop amplification quickly, (b) preserve at-most-once semantics for idempotent requests, and (c) restore degraded tenants without broad rolling restarts.

Why different from prior work: existing fixes centered on adapter-level backoff and proxy tuning; this initiative isolates offending tenant connections at the gateway and provides a transparent replay path that replays safe requests to compatible fallbacks to keep customer applications online while we remediate the root cause. The goal is to reduce blast radius without removing tenant throughput guarantees for unaffected customers.

Scope: hosted API frontends, edge proxy, runtime admission controller, and SDK guidance. Not part of this ticket: Dedicated capacity autoscaling policy changes and Private on-prem packaging (those will follow if telemetry shows similar patterns).
updates: 2026-03-10: Triage call — assigned to Marco. Root-cause hypothesis drafted; customer communication template prepared.
2026-03-11: Captured heap/kv-cache traces from affected workers; isolated a pattern of KV-eviction spikes correlating with high connection resets.
2026-03-12: Prototype quarantine middleware implemented in edge-proxy (branch: github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/tree/feat/tenant-quarantine).
2026-03-13: Canary run started in us-west-2 on a small subset of noisy tenants; observed immediate drop in 5xx amplification for canary group.
2026-03-14: Rollback safeguard and transparent-replay patch merged to main; preparing wider rollout and client SDK advisory.
remediation_steps: 1) Deploy edge-proxy quarantine middleware to canary hosts (us-west-2).
2) Enable transparent replay for requests that include idempotency token or are marked replay-safe by SDK.
3) Throttle new incoming connections for quarantined tenants with exponentially increasing backoff window (starts 200ms).
4) Switch quarantined tenants to a compatible fallback model variant (smaller KV footprint) when available.
5) Run KV-cache compaction job on affected worker pool after quiescing quarantined connections.
6) Monitor canary for 48 hours, then progressively expand region-by-region if no regression.
monitoring_checks: Alert: tenant_quarantine_triggered (severity: P1) — fires when >10% of tenant's connections are quarantined within 5m.
Metric: per-tenant 5xx rate pre/post quarantine (compare 1h windows).
Metric: KV-eviction-rate and cache-hit-rate on worker pool.
SLO check: 99th pct latency for non-quarantined tenants must not regress >10% vs baseline.
Dashboards: canary vs global comparison panels; retry amplification ratio visualization.
postmortem_actions: Root cause doc to be published to Confluence after full roll — include kernel scheduling traces and heap timelines.
Follow-up ticket to add runtime-level admission control to avoid single-tenant KV-cache starvation (ENG-523011).
Update SDKs with clear guidance on idempotency tokens and retry semantics; add sample code and new 'replay-safe' flag.
Run chaos tests simulating rapid retry storms in staging to validate quarantine and replay behavior.
